The Yu-Gi-Oh! Championship Series is steeped in Dueling history and traditions unique to the YCS circuit. Case in point? Bounties! Every YCS weekend sees a handful of competitors dubbed “Bounty Duelists”, making them part of a unique secondary prizing system.

How does it work? Every Round, each Bounty Duelist adds four booster packs to their personal hoard. When they win a Match, the Bounty Duelist gets to claim two of those packs, which are removed from the hoard and theirs to keep. The remaining two packs for the round are added to the hoard, so as long as the Bounty Duelist keeps winning the bounty on their head keeps getting bigger. But if the Bounty Duelist is ever defeated, their opponent claims the whole hoard: so in Round 1 that could be four packs, but in Round 2 it grows to six, Round 3 it grows to eight, and so on.

After 8 Rounds of Swiss play we have the Top 8 of our Ultimate Time Wizard Event! These Duelists took a trip back time to April 2010 to play with some of their favorite cards. They came out on top of 152 other Duelists. Tomorrow, they’ll be playing out Top 8 to see who takes home a giant
card.
The Top 8 are lined up from 1st Place to 8th Place, left to right. We have: Dirk Wagner, Samuel Brouillard, Eric Shen,
(not pictured), Richard Ng, Bradley Bahirathan, Frazier Smith, and Enrique Flores Jr.
Congratulations and good luck to our Top 8 Duelists!

We are in the last Round of Swiss for Day 1 here at YCS Niagara Falls. In the Top Tables right now, we still see mostly Snake-Eye variants. Most of them are running Azamina cards and some of them are playing Fire Kings.
Centur-Ion Bystial and Tenpai are still in the running, along with the Snake-Eye Rescue-ACE Deck. Two Plant Link Decks have made it into the Top Tables and are in the running for Day 2 here!
Yubel, Sky Striker, Runick White Forest, and Gimmick Puppet are all also in the Top Tables and are in the contention to make Day 2 this weekend.
With just one Round left of Swiss, roughly half the floor is Snake-Eye variants while rest are assorted strategies, we’ll have to wait and see what makes it to Day 2 here at YCS Niagara Falls!

from Trenton, NJ has judged almost a dozen YCS events, but never played in one until today! He’s very excited about finally competing. “I like the pressure that it brings,” he said. “You feel it in the days leading up to the event.” He also said that looking around the venue and seeing so many well-known players increases the pressure. “I welcome the challenge as a player,” he said. For all of the events he has judged, Kyree says he is excited to finally experience an event from the players’ perspective. “I welcome learning what the players have to go through,” he said. “I wanted to experience how the judges and staff treat the players so I can better understand the players’ perspectives.” Kyree used a Traptrix Deck this weekend, and even though he didn’t fare well with it, he didn’t let that get him down. “I’ve met some amazing players in the community,” he said. “I’ve won some gams, lost some games, and am making friends.” He’s excited to connect with people this weekend, and to enjoy the full experience of attending YCS Niagara Falls.

Brendan O’Shea from Ireland is in Canada visiting friends, and now he’s competing in his first YCS this weekend! He likes the Public Events best. “I like being able to win Game Mats and all of the prizes,” he said. Brendan is impressed by the amount of space in the tournament hall, and excited about facing off against lots of different Duelists. “I played against the Head Judge of Ireland’s National Championship in Round 2 of the YCS,” he said. “I never spoke to him until today, even though I saw him at the National Championship.” It’s always exciting to Duel against players you’ve seen, but don’t really know well.
